About Us
Redbridge Alternative Provision (RAP) is a school that provides support for pupils who have been, or who are at risk of, permanent exclusion from mainstream schools. The school has a separate provision (YEP) for up to 65 Year 11 pupils, who are new to the country, many of whom arrived unaccompanied.
At RAP we aim to provide a high-quality education which is tailored, inclusive and inspiring for young people who are at risk of permanent exclusion or for those who have been permanently excluded. Running parallel to this is a programme of wrap-around pastoral care ensuring our students’ emotional and social needs are met.
Students are challenged to take responsibility, modify their behaviour, improve attitudes to school life and make academic progress across the range and breadth of curriculum opportunities available. In addition to classroom-based learning, students are provided with enrichment opportunities throughout the academic year.
We respect that all our young people are individuals from a diverse range of backgrounds and life-experiences. We passionately believe that by assisting them to overcome their personal barriers they should be entitled to access the full range of opportunities available in society.

“In my world, there are no bad kids, just impressionable, conflicted young people wrestling with emotions and impulses, trying to communicate their feelings and needs the only way they know how.”

Enrichment
In addition to following the National Curriculum at RAP, we have a comprehensive Enrichment Programme to enhance students’ learning opportunities and help pupils develop emotionally and socially. This programme allows students to develop their inter-personal skills and self-image, improve social skills, and build friendships. The Enrichment Programme is an opportunity for students’ learning experiences to be extended into the community and expose them to experiences they would not have ordinarily outside of school.
Box Up Gym provides a highly structured and disciplined environment where routines, focus and self-control are central. For students at RAP, many of whom have identified SEMH needs linked to impulsivity, emotional regulation or difficulty managing boundaries, the predictable structure of each session provides stability and clarity. Clear expectations and repetition support students to regulate emotions, manage frustration and respond positively to challenge, skills that directly support reintegration into mainstream education.
Climbing activities challenge students to assess risk, plan routes and persevere through difficulty. Students learn to manage fear, accept support and reflect on progress. Overcoming physical and mental challenges reinforces a growth mindset and builds confidence, supporting positive attitudes to learning and resilience in mainstream classrooms.
Cycling sessions develop co-ordination, independence and responsibility through structured physical activity. Students follow safety guidance, manage equipment and remain aware of others, reinforcing accountability and focus. These behaviours support students in developing routines and self-management skills that transfer directly to school life.
Exploration and Ecology activities encourage curiosity, responsibility and environmental awareness through practical learning. Students work collaboratively and engage in observation and reflection, supporting confidence, engagement and respect for shared spaces.
Nature walks at Forest Country Park and Farm provide calm, structured opportunities for reflection and emotional regulation. Alongside guided walks, students take part in activities such as strawberry picking and fishing, which offer hands-on, low-pressure experiences that support anxiety reduction, self-awareness and patience. These activities help students develop focus, emotional balance and confidence, contributing positively to their readiness to engage with classroom learning.
The Future Ready programme supports students to develop confidence, self-awareness and practical skills through a balance of creative and wellbeing-focused activities. The programme provides structured opportunities for students to re-engage with learning in ways that feel accessible and purposeful.
Creative elements, including pottery workshops, offer calm, hands-on experiences that support focus, emotional regulation and self-expression. Working at an individual pace helps reduce anxiety, while producing a finished piece builds pride and a sense of achievement.
By linking creativity with wellbeing and routine, Future Ready supports students in developing resilience and positive habits that strengthen readiness to re-engage with mainstream education.
Gym sessions provide students at RAP with structured opportunities to build healthy routines, set personal goals and support both physical and mental wellbeing. For students with SEMH needs, developing consistent routines and understanding the link between physical activity, mood and focus supports emotional regulation and resilience. These habits help students establish positive behaviours that improve engagement and readiness to return to mainstream education.
Gymnastics sessions focus on co-ordination, strength and controlled movement while reinforcing discipline and focus. Students follow structured routines and refine techniques over time, promoting patience and self-regulation. These skills support improved engagement and behaviour in structured learning environments.
Ice skating places students in an unfamiliar setting that requires patience, balance and perseverance. Students are supported to manage frustration, accept guidance and persist through challenge. Developing confidence in unfamiliar environments and learning to cope with setbacks supports resilience and adaptability, which are essential for sustained engagement when returning to mainstream settings.
Visits to Lambourne End provide students with practical outdoor challenges that promote teamwork, communication and independence. For students at RAP, these experiences offer structured opportunities to practise cooperation, follow instructions and trust others in a safe environment. Successfully completing activities builds confidence and self-belief, supporting students to engage more positively with group learning and social expectations in mainstream schools.
Roller Skating encourages perseverance, confidence and gradual skill development. Students are supported to manage initial difficulty and recognise progress over time. These experiences reinforce resilience and willingness to engage with unfamiliar learning experiences, supporting confidence on return to mainstream education.
Tennis and Padel sessions promote teamwork, communication and respect through structured sport. Students learn to follow rules, manage competition and cooperate with peers. These sessions support positive social interaction and emotional control, reinforcing behaviours expected in mainstream school settings.

A message from our Headteacher
Dear Students, Parents, Staff, and Community Members,
I am delighted to welcome you to Redbridge Alternative Provision (RAP) , a place where every student is valued and encouraged to achieve their full potential.
RAP is a school that provides support for pupils who have been, or who are at risk of, permanent exclusion from mainstream schools. The school has a separate provision (YEP) for up to 65 Year 11 pupils, who are new to the country, many of whom arrived unaccompanied. It also has a Vocational provision (RAPv) where pupils can complete vocational qualifications including Construction.
At RAP, our mission is to provide a supportive and nurturing environment where students can thrive academically, socially, and emotionally. We understand that each student is unique, and we are committed to offering tailored educational experiences that meet their individual needs.
About Me
My name is Rubert Jonker, and I bring with me over 20 years of experience in both mainstream and special schools. For the past 11 years, I have served as a senior leader and deputy headteacher in specialist settings. I am also an Advanced SENCO and have achieved the National Professional Qualification for Headship (NPQH). My journey in education has been driven by a deep passion for ensuring that all students, regardless of their background or circumstances, have access to high-quality education and the support they need to succeed.
On a personal note, I have also had the honour of playing international and professional rugby league, which has instilled in me the values of teamwork, resilience, and dedication—qualities that I aim to bring to our school community.
Our Vision and Goals
Our vision at Redbridge Alternative Provision is to create a community where:
Every student feels safe, respected, and valued.
Commitment to Excellence
We are dedicated to maintaining a standard of excellence in all aspects of our provision. This includes:
Looking Ahead
As we move forward, I am eager to work collaboratively with our talented staff, supportive parents, and dedicated students. Together, we can build on our strengths and address any challenges, ensuring that RAP continues to be a place where every student can flourish.
Should you have any questions or wish to get involved, please do not hesitate to contact us.
Thank you for your warm welcome, and I look forward to meeting you all.
Mr Rubert Jonker Headteacher

Therapeutic Support
Redbridge Alternative Provision (RAP) offers a comprehensive range of universal and targeted support and interventions across the school. Our therapeutic support is tailored to meet each student’s individual social, emotional, and mental health needs, ensuring a bespoke approach that responds effectively to their specific circumstances.
At RAP, we recognise that one size does not fit all. There are times when a student may require support that is additional to, and different from, the universal offer in order to access learning successfully.
The Universal Offer at RAP includes:
Interventions to enable a student to better access the curriculum may include:
Where a student’s primary barrier to learning is that they are emotionally unavailable to learn, a range of therapeutic supports and interventions are available. In most cases, these are delivered through a graduated response, with the level of support increasing in frequency and or intensity according to need.
Constant positive regard.
Small class sizes.
A high adult-to-student ratio.
High-quality careers information, advice, and guidance.
Equal access and opportunity for all students.
A visual timetable.
Alternative teaching approaches.
Adapted learning resources and materials.
Additional Learning Support (ALS).
1:1 support.
Further diagnostic assessment e.g. Dyslexia.
Speech & Language support.
Therapeutic Support – a graduated response
Behaviour Mentors work closely with students to address current and potential barriers to learning through supportive 1:1 relationships. They support students to develop coping strategies, increase motivation, raise aspirations, and re-engage with education.
Mentors recognise that difficulties with learning and behaviour often stem from complex underlying factors such as bereavement, low self-esteem, mental health needs, family circumstances, peer relationships, bullying, or substance misuse. They provide students with a trusted adult who listens and supports them in navigating these challenges.
Behaviour Mentors develop individual action plans with students, work closely with parents and carers, and liaise with external professionals where appropriate, including Social Workers, Youth Offending Service workers, and Education Welfare Officers.
Our Behaviour Mentors are Mr Akoto and Mr Boafo.
The Sensory Room provides students with a safe and calming environment to manage stress and anxiety, particularly when school feels overwhelming. It supports emotional regulation through sensory breaks, movement, and tactile activities, helping students to regain control and re-engage with learning.
The space also promotes communication and social skills through guided activities and co-operative play. Sensory provision is particularly beneficial for students with Autism, ADHD, sensory processing differences, or anxiety, and can be adapted to meet a student’s individual needs.
Art Therapy is delivered through 1:1 sessions and provides a structured therapeutic approach for students who have experienced exclusion and may struggle with behaviour, confidence, or engagement.
Students work with a wide range of creative materials, including drawing, painting, collage, sculpture, and mixed media. Sessions are designed to encourage exploration, creativity, and experimentation within a safe and supportive setting.
Through the creative process, students develop self-confidence, focus, resilience, and emotional expression, supporting improved engagement with school and everyday life.
Reset Time provides students with a short, supervised opportunity to step away from the classroom when they are feeling overwhelmed. This allows students to reflect, co-regulate with an adult, and manage their emotions before returning to learning.
It is a proactive strategy designed to reduce escalation, support emotional regulation, and minimise disruption to the learning of others. Reset Time is supervised by the Pastoral Team, with support from Behaviour Mentors. Students are listened to, supported to regulate, provided with appropriate work, and supported to return to lessons when ready.
Children who are looked after by the Local Authority, or who have recent experiences of care, often experience trauma related to attachment, separation, loss, bereavement, and identity. These experiences can significantly impact emotional wellbeing and availability to learn.
Where capacity allows and where required, these students are provided with targeted therapeutic support from the Pastoral Team, SENCO, and Behaviour Mentors to support emotional development and long-term outcomes.

Curriculum
At RAP we intend to inspire curiosity and provide abundant opportunities to obtain knowledge and understanding so that students acquire meaningful functional literacy and numeracy skills, become lifelong learners, are able to ask for help when needed and are able to make informed choices.
We aim to equip students with the attitudes and skills to become successful citizens so that they know how to keep themselves safe, have healthy friendships and relationships, are able to regulate their own behaviour and can express themselves clearly and coherently.
We strive to ensure students gain qualifications that are relevant and for their future aspirations so that they achieve their full academic potential, understand the options available for their future, are ready to seek employment and are able to manage their finances.
Key Stage 3 In Years 7 to 9 students study the following subjects: English, Mathematics, Science, History, Geography, Food Technology, Art, PE and PSHE.
For students permanently excluded from school during Key Stage 4 every attempt is made to put in place a bespoke timetable so that they can continue on study programme they have started, though this is not always possible. In Years 10 and 11 students study the core curriculum of English (GCSE and Functional Skills), Mathematics (GCSE and Functional Skills) and Science (GCSE). Students can study additional qualifications such as:
Food Technology (GCSE/BTEC)
Sport Science (BTEC)
Travel & Tourism (BTEC)

Cultural Capital
Within a school setting, Cultural Capital is defined as ‘the essential knowledge that students need to be educated citizens, introducing them to the best that has been thought and said and helping to engender an appreciation of human creativity and achievement.
At RAP we place a huge importance on providing students with endless opportunities to develop their Cultural Capital. Such Cultural Capital opportunities can be seen through a range of trips and school visits linked to each of the curriculum areas. Further to this there are a range of themed weeks/celebrations, reward trips, residential experiences and a variety of opportunities to take part in activities that pupils wouldn’t ordinarily take part in, all aimed at enriching their lives.
Cultural Capital opportunities at RAP have been carefully sequenced to ensure that they are progressive year-on-year and prepare students to be understanding and a contributing member of society. Click on the links below to download each year groups Cultural Capital scheduled events.

Reading at RAP
At Redbridge Alternative Provision (RAP), we recognise reading as the foundation of learning, independence, and future success. Many of our students arrive with disrupted educational experiences, social, emotional and mental health needs, and low confidence as learners. As a result, reading is central to our school improvement strategy.
We aim for all students to become confident, fluent readers who can access the curriculum, engage with a wide range of texts, and succeed in education, employment, or training. Alongside this, we strive to foster a positive reading culture, helping students to see reading as purposeful, relevant, and enjoyable.
Reading is embedded across the curriculum and wider school life. Through initiatives such as Poetry Week and Literacy Week, students are given opportunities to engage with language creatively, develop their voice, and build positive relationships with reading.
As students progress, we develop their ability to read with increasing fluency, understanding, and critical awareness, ensuring they are equipped with the skills needed to thrive beyond RAP.
Students will develop the confidence to use reading as a tool for learning and for life.
When students join RAP, they are assessed using Star Reader and other standardised assessments to identify their reading age and specific areas of need. This ensures that teaching and intervention are tailored to each student’s starting point.
Reading development is supported through a structured, whole-school approach. All students access timetabled Literacy for Life lessons, alongside regular opportunities for reading in form time and across the curriculum. Accelerated Reader is used to guide book choices, support comprehension, and track progress, enabling students to take ownership of their reading journey.
Students requiring additional support receive targeted intervention through the Additional Learning Support programme. This provision is bespoke and may focus on phonics, fluency, comprehension, or vocabulary development, depending on individual need. Reading data is used consistently by staff to adapt teaching, provide appropriate challenge, and ensure progress is closely monitored.
The development of the RAP library further supports reading for pleasure, offering a range of diverse and engaging texts matched to students’ interests and reading levels. Whole-school initiatives, including Poetry Week and Literacy Week, promote reading as a shared and valued part of school life, helping to build confidence and engagement
Our approach ensures that students make measurable progress from their individual starting points and develop as confident, capable readers.
Students demonstrate:
Reading becomes both a skill and a source of enjoyment. Students begin to see themselves as readers, developing resilience, self-esteem, and a stronger connection to learning.
At Key Stage 4, students are better prepared for Functional Skills and GCSE-style reading demands, with outcomes reflecting the impact of targeted, data-informed provision.
Ultimately, students transition from reluctant or disengaged readers to motivated learners who can use reading to succeed in education and beyond.
Improved reading ages and comprehension skills
Increased confidence and engagement with texts
Enhanced ability to access learning across subjects

Year 8
Subject Intent
English
At RAP, the Key Stage 3 English curriculum intends to develop students into curious readers capable of accessing a broad variety of texts and genres from the literary canon. When it comes to writing, students will engage in creative expression, confidently employing a range of sentence structures and complex vocabulary. Furthermore, our goal is to empower students to become proficient speakers, capable of presenting ideas in a formal context, actively listening to feedback, and asking questions to clarify information—all while using standard English. Through a skills-based curriculum, we aim for pupils to practice speaking and listening with consideration for a specific audience, effectively communicate and formulate their own opinions, and engage in active listening and appropriate responses. Students will continue to develop into confident individuals who excel in these language skills.
Mathematics
At RAP, the Key Stage 3 maths curriculum intends to embed key mathematical skills so that students can become fluent in the fundamentals of mathematics, reason mathematically, and problem solve by applying their skills and knowledge. We intend to expand students’ range of mathematical competencies so that they have a greater understanding of Maths in real life. This will in turn give them the skills to develop their confidence to make decisions about their money, time, and freedom as they prepare for adulthood.
Science
At RAP, the Key Stage 3 science curriculum aims to cultivate curiosity and foster an inquisitive mindset about the universe among our students. At this stage, there is a fundamental shift from the science lessons experienced in primary school. Our goal is to encourage students to actively participate in a variety of practical work, gradually bridging connections between practical work and theoretical concepts. The lessons are structured around developing scientific inquiry skills, including classifying, comparing and contrasting, predicting, making models, gathering data, measuring, and observing. We intend to build upon and deepen students’ scientific knowledge, emphasising their understanding of ideas and concepts developed in the earlier Key Stages, particularly in the disciplines of Biology, Chemistry, and Physics.
Art
At RAP, the Key Stage 3 art curriculum intends to develop students’ critical and analytical abilities whilst giving them the opportunity to express themselves freely. The curriculum intends for students to build on prior learning and develop their confidence and knowledge of working with different materials and processes, to analyse their own work and the works of famous artists and designers, both contemporary and historical. This will help them to express their own creativity, ideas and investigations through the medium of art. Students will gain perseverance skills from self-analysis helping them to decide if they want to continue their journey into Key Stage 4 Art.
Food Technology
At RAP, the Key Stage 3 food technology curriculum intends to provide a comprehensive exploration of the food we consume. The curriculum aims to equip all students with the understanding and confidence to create their own dishes from scratch. Through hands-on experiences, students will explore different textures, flavours and cooking styles. The curriculum aims for students to understand the importance of food and its role in improving overall health and wellbeing.
Geography
At RAP, The Key Stage 3 geography curriculum intends to inform students about the enormity of our world. The curriculum encourages students to use maps and atlases so that pupils can develop an understanding of different countries, continents, seas and oceans. Through studying the natural and human environments, as well as physical and human processes, the curriculum aims to provide students with a sense of awe and wonder about the world they live in, building a sense of curiosity and asking questions so that they are keen to continue learning about the world in Key Stage 3.
History
At RAP, the Key Stage 3 history curriculum intends to foster a deep understanding of historical events, cultures and individuals, cultivating critical thinking skills among students. By exploring diverse perspectives and analysing primary sources, the History curriculum strives to develop a sense of historical empathy. It intends to instil a passion for inquiry, encouraging students to question, investigate and draw connections between past and present. The aim is to empower learners with the knowledge and skills necessary for informed citizenship, promoting an appreciation for the complexities and nuances of history.
PE
At RAP, the Key Stage 3 PE curriculum intends to adhere to the philosophy of ‘Sport for All’. The school aims to deliver an exciting and enjoyable experience for all students acquiring the skills and knowledge in line with the National Curriculum. The broad and balanced curriculum aims to re-cap, re-call and build on prior knowledge using a range of physical activities. Through a carefully structured programme, we aim for students to build their physical, social and mental skills, enabling them to fully participate in a range of roles in PE. All students at RAP have the opportunity to participate in an extensive Extra Curricular/Enrichment programme, which develops students’ confidence in applying their skills in competitive situations.
PSHE/RSE
At RAP, the Key Stage 3 PSHE curriculum intends to empower students with the knowledge, skills and attribute development to equip them to enjoy healthy relationships and navigate the wider world as happy, healthy and fulfilled teenagers. The curriculum focuses on the use of distanced and experiential learning opportunities to engage pupils and meet age, stage and SEMH needs, whilst developing students’ moral compass. Students are supported to navigate challenges by responding to spontaneous issues both in our school community and the wider world. As part of the PHSE curriculum, students are taught RSE to foster an understanding and respect of different faiths and diversity within the community. The curriculum intends to ensure our students practice skills to access reliable information and support services linked to each topic area. Parents have the statutory right to withdraw their child from the sex education element of the RSE curriculum.

Year 11
Subject Intent
English
In Year 11 the English Language and Literature curriculum is designed to introduce students to a rich and diverse range of texts that challenge, inspire, and cultivate lifelong readers. Our skills-based approach equips students with the tools and knowledge needed to confidently articulate and express their thoughts, ideas, and emotions on a variety of topics, both verbally and in writing, to a wide range of audiences.
Students are encouraged to engage with thought-provoking questions and develop the ability to shape these ideas into meaningful, well-structured, and analytical pieces of writing. Through the exploration of varied themes and perspectives, the curriculum broadens students’ understanding of the world around them and deepens their critical thinking skills.
Alongside preparation for GCSE English Language and English Literature, students can gain Entry Level and equivalent qualifications (Functional Skills) where appropriate, ensuring that all learners are supported and able to achieve success. By fostering a shared passion for English, we aim to ignite a love of reading and writing that extends beyond the classroom and into everyday life.
Mathematics
In Year 11 the maths curriculum is designed to ensure that all students develop fluency in mathematical reasoning and problem solving, preparing them for everyday life and future employment. We aim to equip students with the mathematical and numerical skills they need to thrive academically and function confidently and successfully in society.
Through a structured and supportive approach, students build fluency, enabling them to select appropriate strategies, reason mathematically, and apply their knowledge to solve a range of problems. The curriculum is tailored to meet individual needs, ensuring that students are equipped with the skills required for their chosen personal pathways.
Alongside preparation for GCSE Mathematics, pupils can achieve equivalent qualifications, including Functional Skills. This ensures that learners of all abilities are supported to make excellent progress, achieve recognised qualifications, and fulfil their potential.
Science
In Year 11 the science curriculum aims to ignite curiosity and develop an inquisitive understanding of the world around us. Through engaging and structured lessons, students build essential scientific enquiry skills, including classifying, comparing, predicting, modelling, gathering and analysing data, measuring accurately, and making informed observations.
The curriculum is designed to consolidate and deepen knowledge introduced at earlier Key Stages, strengthening students’ understanding of key scientific ideas and concepts. Science is delivered across the disciplines of Biology, Chemistry, and Physics, enabling students to explore different areas of the subject and develop their individual interests and strengths.
Alongside preparation for GCSE Science, pupils can achieve equivalent qualifications where appropriate. Studying Science at Key Stage 4 provides students with a strong foundation for further education, training, and a wide range of future career pathways.
Art
In Year 11 the art curriculum is designed to develop students’ resilience, confidence, and creativity through sustained independent exploration of materials, techniques, processes, and personal ideas. Students are encouraged to experiment, take creative risks, and express themselves imaginatively and inventively within a supportive environment.
Throughout the course, students refine their practical skills while learning to contextualise and critically analyse both historical and contemporary art. This ensures their work is informed, purposeful, and reflective, leading to a meaningful and enriching artistic experience.
Students will sit GCSE Art, building a strong portfolio that demonstrates their technical ability, creativity, and critical understanding. The curriculum also supports students in recognising the wide range of progression pathways available within the arts, while gaining insight into the significant role art plays in shaping culture and society today
Food Technology
In Year 11 the food technology curriculum builds on students’ knowledge and practical skills, with an increased focus on independence, application and assessment. Students refine their cooking, planning, food safety and evaluation skills while applying their understanding to realistic hospitality and catering scenarios. The curriculum prepares students to successfully achieve BTEC Home Cooking Skills and WJEC Hospitality and Catering qualifications and supports progression into further education, training and employment.
History
In Year 11 the history curriculum intends to refine students’ historical understanding, critical analysis and independent research skills. Students are encouraged to explore connections, causation and differing perspectives. Through engaging with primary and secondary sources, the curriculum intends to cultivate a nuanced appreciation for historical contexts. Additionally, the curriculum aims to prepare students for further academic pursuits and instil a sense of historical curiosity. This will empower pupils to navigate the complexities of the modern world with a well-informed historical perspective, allowing them to achieve a recognised qualification.
Music
In Year 11 the music curriculum intends to not only focus on helping pupils to express themselves creatively through performance and composition but also includes preparing pupils for music industry careers. This comprehensive program ensures pupils not only cultivate a thorough understanding of music but also acquire practical skills, providing them with the essential knowledge for successful endeavours in the dynamic music industry. The curriculum aims to empower pupils with a well-rounded musical education that prepares them for a variety of opportunities and challenges; all whilst gaining a BTEC qualification. The curriculum aims to empower pupils with a well-rounded musical education that prepares them for a variety of opportunities and challenges; all whilst gaining a BTEC qualification.
PE
In Year 11 the PE curriculum is underpinned by the philosophy of ‘Sport for All’. We are committed to delivering an engaging and enjoyable experience for every student, enabling them to acquire the skills and knowledge in line with the National Curriculum.
Through a carefully structured programme, students develop their physical, social, and mental skills, allowing them to participate confidently in a variety of roles within Physical Education. The curriculum promotes teamwork, resilience, leadership, and sportsmanship, while building confidence in applying skills effectively within competitive situations.
Alongside their practical development, pupils have the opportunity to gain a GCSE equivalent qualification, ensuring they achieve recognised accreditation while fostering a lifelong appreciation for physical activity and healthy living.
PSHE/RSE
In Year 11 the PSHE/RSE curriculum is designed to develop pupils’ knowledge, skills, and personal attributes to support a healthy, safe, and successful transition into adulthood. Pupils explore their own attitudes, values, and beliefs while developing an understanding of other people’s perspectives. The curriculum incorporates both distanced and experiential learning opportunities, allowing pupils to practice managing influence and risk and to make informed decisions about health, relationships, financial capability, future learning, and employability.
RSE is included within the PSHE program to encourage respect and understanding of different faiths and the diversity within the community. By engaging with a range of beliefs and perspectives, pupils develop empathy and the skills needed to navigate complex social environments.
The curriculum is designed to prepare pupils for life in the modern world, equipping them to live as happy, healthy, and fulfilled adults who can successfully navigate diverse and ever-changing communities and workplaces. Parents have the statutory right to withdraw their child from the sex education element of the RSE curriculum.
Travel and Tourism
In Year 11 the travel and tourism curriculum intends to develop students’ ability to apply their knowledge confidently and independently. Students will explore customer experiences and the social, economic, political, technological and environmental influences affecting global tourism. Through contemporary case studies and vocational scenarios, students will strengthen their analytical and evaluative skills, prepare for assessment and develop knowledge that supports progression into further education, training and employment.

Subject Intent
English
At RAP, the Key Stage 3 English curriculum intends to develop students into curious readers capable of accessing a broad variety of texts and genres from the literary canon. When it comes to writing, students will engage in creative expression, confidently employing a range of sentence structures and complex vocabulary. Furthermore, our goal is to empower students to become proficient speakers, capable of presenting ideas in a formal context, actively listening to feedback, and asking questions to clarify information—all while using standard English. Through a skills-based curriculum, we aim for pupils to practice speaking and listening with consideration for a specific audience, effectively communicate and formulate their own opinions, and engage in active listening and appropriate responses. Students will continue to develop into confident individuals who excel in these language skills.
Mathematics
At RAP, the Key Stage 3 maths curriculum intends to embed key mathematical skills so that students can become fluent in the fundamentals of mathematics, reason mathematically, and problem solve by applying their skills and knowledge. We intend to expand students’ range of mathematical competencies so that they have a greater understanding of Maths in real life. This will in turn give them the skills to develop their confidence to make decisions about their money, time, and freedom as they prepare for adulthood.
Science
At RAP, the Key Stage 3 science curriculum aims to cultivate curiosity and foster an inquisitive mindset about the universe among our students. At this stage, there is a fundamental shift from the science lessons experienced in primary school. Our goal is to encourage students to actively participate in a variety of practical work, gradually bridging connections between practical work and theoretical concepts. The lessons are structured around developing scientific inquiry skills, including classifying, comparing and contrasting, predicting, making models, gathering data, measuring, and observing. We intend to build upon and deepen students’ scientific knowledge, emphasising their understanding of ideas and concepts developed in the earlier Key Stages, particularly in the disciplines of Biology, Chemistry, and Physics.
Art
At RAP, the Key Stage 3 art curriculum intends to develop students’ critical and analytical abilities whilst giving them the opportunity to express themselves freely. The curriculum intends for students to build on prior learning and develop their confidence and knowledge of working with different materials and processes, to analyse their own work and the works of famous artists and designers, both contemporary and historical. This will help them to express their own creativity, ideas and investigations through the medium of art. Students will gain perseverance skills from self-analysis helping them to decide if they want to continue their journey into Key Stage 4 Art.
Food Technology
At RAP, the Key Stage 3 food technology curriculum intends to provide a comprehensive exploration of the food we consume. The curriculum aims to equip all students with the understanding and confidence to create their own dishes from scratch. Through hands-on experiences, students will explore different textures, flavours and cooking styles. The curriculum aims for students to understand the importance of food and its role in improving overall health and wellbeing.
Geography
At RAP, the Key Stage 3 geography curriculum intends to inform students about the enormity of our world. The curriculum encourages students to use maps and atlases so that pupils can develop an understanding of different countries, continents, seas and oceans. Through studying the natural and human environments, as well as physical and human processes, the curriculum aims to provide students with a sense of awe and wonder about the world they live in, building a sense of curiosity and asking questions so that they are keen to continue learning about the world in Key Stage 3.
History
At RAP, the Key Stage 3 history curriculum intends to foster a deep understanding of historical events, cultures and individuals, cultivating critical thinking skills among students. By exploring diverse perspectives and analysing primary sources, the History curriculum strives to develop a sense of historical empathy. It intends to instil a passion for inquiry, encouraging students to question, investigate and draw connections between past and present. The aim is to empower learners with the knowledge and skills necessary for informed citizenship, promoting an appreciation for the complexities and nuances of history.
PE
At RAP, the Key Stage 3 PE curriculum intends to adhere to the philosophy of ‘Sport for All’. The school aims to deliver an exciting and enjoyable experience for all students acquiring the skills and knowledge in line with the National Curriculum. The broad and balanced curriculum aims to re-cap, re-call and build on prior knowledge using a range of physical activities. Through a carefully structured programme, we aim for students to build their physical, social and mental skills, enabling them to fully participate in a range of roles in PE. All students at RAP have the opportunity to participate in an extensive Extra Curricular/Enrichment programme, which develops students’ confidence in applying their skills in competitive situations.
PSHE/RSE
At RAP, the Key Stage 3 PSHE curriculum intends to empower students with the knowledge, skills and attribute development to equip them to enjoy healthy relationships and navigate the wider world as happy, healthy and fulfilled teenagers. The curriculum focuses on the use of distanced and experiential learning opportunities to engage pupils and meet age, stage and SEMH needs, whilst developing students’ moral compass. Students are supported to navigate challenges by responding to spontaneous issues both in our school community and the wider world. As part of the PHSE curriculum, students are taught RSE to foster an understanding and respect of different faiths and diversity within the community. The curriculum intends to ensure our students practice skills to access reliable information and support services linked to each topic area. Parents have the statutory right to withdraw their child from the sex education element of the RSE curriculum.

Careers Education, Information, Advice and Guidance (CEIAG)
At RAP we are committed to providing all our students from Years 7 to 11 with a wide-ranging programme of careers education, information, advice and guidance (CEIAG) . We firmly believe that outstanding careers education is one of the driving forces behind social mobility and therefore our aspiring careers programme is an integral part of the offer provided to our pupils.
Throughout Year 7-9 all pupils will have had the opportunity to:
Throughout Year 10-11 all pupils will have had the opportunity to:
Career Guidance Meetings Pupils are entitled to appropriate guidance to meet their individual needs. All pupils at school can request an appointment with the Pupil Pathways Coordinator, although Year 10 & 11 will have scheduled half termly appointments. Pupils are identified for careers meetings based on need and through self-referral.
Career information Career information is available through relevant displays and through assemblies. Students at RAP will have access to a range of career guides, apprenticeship and employer information, as well as guides on job-search activities.
External providers Ranges of external providers are invited into school to support the careers programme. These might include local colleges, universities, training providers, apprenticeship organisations, employers, school alumni, or staff from various projects.
Employer links Links with employers, businesses and other external agencies continue to grow by building on local community connections with a view to offer pupils experience in the world of work.
Careers Education in the Curriculum PSHE is offered to all pupils in Year 7 – Year 11 and within this there is explicit careers guidance and units of work designed to support all pupils in their destinations. Careers, information and guidance will also permeate throughout the wider school curriculum enabling pupils to link their learning to a range of potential future career pathways.
As students in Year 11 are approaching the period when they are choosing their Post 16 options, it is important for students to attend as many open days in colleges and sixth forms they might be interested in. Attending an open day gives you the chance to hear from those already at the college/sixth and talk about their experiences, along with what you can expect when you leave school. They may shed light on an important part of the university experience you hadn’t even thought to consider.
Gatsby Benchmark The Gatsby Benchmark is a framework which is used by the school to assess the development of our students’ employability skills.
Our Careers Team are guided by the 8 benchmarks to provide our pupils with the best careers education, information, advice and guidance.
To view how we apply the benchmarks, click on the link below:
